bss.topic: Pontos de referência e trajetos: de casa à escola

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que é um ponto de referência?
options: Um lugar fácil de reconhecer que ajuda a se localizar
questions.answer: Um lugar fácil de reconhecer que ajuda a se localizar
questions.hint: Pense em algo que você vê e reconhece no caminho.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como chamamos o caminho que fazemos de um lugar até outro?
questions.hint: Começa com a letra T.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destes é um bom ponto de referência no caminho para a escola?
questions.hint: Um bom ponto de referência fica sempre no mesmo lugar.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que um carro estacionado NÃO é um bom ponto de referência?
options: Porque ele pode sair do lugar
questions.answer: Porque ele pode sair do lugar
questions.hint: Ele vai estar lá amanhã?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Lia diz: 'Minha casa fica ao lado da farmácia.' Qual é o ponto de referência?
questions.hint: O que ajuda a achar a casa?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual palavra completa a frase? 'A escola fica ___ da praça, do outro lado da rua.'
questions.hint: Do outro lado da rua, olhando para ela.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Tomás sai de casa, vira à direita e anda até a igreja. Para que lado ele virou?
questions.hint: Leia de novo a frase.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Complete: para descrever um trajeto, usamos palavras como 'vire à direita' e 'vire à ___'.
questions.hint: É o contrário de direita.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destas frases descreve melhor um trajeto?
options: Saio de casa, passo pelo mercado e viro na esquina da escola.
Eu gosto muito da minha escola.
A escola tem um pátio grande.
questions.answer: Saio de casa, passo pelo mercado e viro na esquina da escola.
questions.hint: Procure a frase que mostra o caminho passo a passo.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Bia passa pela padaria e depois pelo parque. O que ela vê primeiro?
questions.hint: Preste atenção na palavra 'depois'.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destes pontos de referência é mais fácil de ver de longe?
questions.hint: Pense no tamanho.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: No mapa de um bairro, a escola está ao norte da casa de Davi. Para chegar lá, Davi anda para o:
questions.hint: A escola está em qual direção?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Para que serve um mapa do caminho até a escola?
options: Para mostrar o trajeto e os pontos de referência
questions.answer: Para mostrar o trajeto e os pontos de referência

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Rafa diz: 'Moro perto do mercado.' Por que é melhor dizer 'Moro na rua do mercado, na casa amarela'?
options: Porque dá mais pistas para achar a casa
questions.answer: Porque dá mais pistas para achar a casa
questions.hint: Mais detalhes ajudam ou atrapalham?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Descreva o trajeto de casa até a escola usando dois pontos de referência.
questions.hint: Diga por onde você passa e para que lado vira.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que é importante conhecer o caminho de casa até a escola?
questions.hint: Pense em segurança e em não se perder.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What does it mean to proof-read your writing?
options: Read it aloud to a friend only
questions.hint: Think about looking for errors.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What do we call the first, rough copy of a piece of writing?
questions.hint: It begins with 'd'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word is spelt correctly?
questions.hint: Say it slowly: be-cause.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: fr_ _nd
questions.hint: There is a sneaky 'i' before 'e' in this word.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is missing from this sentence? 'where is my coat'
options: a capital letter and a question mark
questions.answer: a capital letter and a question mark
questions.hint: Is it asking something?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word is a better choice than 'nice' in: 'We had a nice day at the beach.'?
questions.hint: Choose a word that shows how good it was.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses commas in a list correctly?
options: I packed a hat, a coat and some gloves.
I packed a hat a coat, and, some gloves.
I packed, a hat a coat and some gloves.
questions.answer: I packed a hat, a coat and some gloves.
questions.hint: Commas go between the items in the list.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word could replace 'said' to show someone was very loud?
questions.hint: Think of a loud voice.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: How can you improve this sentence? 'The cat sat.'
options: The fluffy cat sat on the warm rug.
questions.answer: The fluffy cat sat on the warm rug.
questions.hint: Adding adjectives and 'where' gives more detail.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word joins these two ideas best? 'I was cold ___ I put on my jumper.'
questions.hint: One thing happened because of the other.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: A draft says: 'Then we ate lunch. Then we went home. Then we slept.' What is the best way to improve it?
options: Use different time words like 'After that' and 'Finally'
questions.answer: Use different time words like 'After that' and 'Finally'
questions.hint: Too many repeated words can sound boring.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 5 misspelled words.
questions.answer: Saterday → Saturday; bilt → built; towr → tower; strawbery → strawberry; hom → home
questions.text: On Saterday, my family went to the seaside. The sun was shining and the water was warm. My little sister bilt a huge sandcastle with a tall towr. Then we had ice cream, and mine was strawbery. It was the best day ever and I did not want to go hom.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write one sentence about your weekend, then improve it by adding an adjective and a joining word.
questions.hint: Try words like 'because', 'and' or 'so'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.hint: Look at the first letter and the last mark.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word in this sentence needs a capital letter? 'on friday we went swimming.'
questions.hint: Days of the week and the first word need capitals.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 4 misspelled words.
questions.answer: droped → dropped; mornin → morning; apeared → appeared; sunlite → sunlight
questions.text: Last week our class planted seeds in the school garden. We dug small holes and droped one seed in each. Every mornin we gave them some water. After a few days, tiny green shoots apeared. Our teacher said they need sunlite to grow. I can't wait to see the flowers.

en_read.topic: Mystery stories: asking questions to understand

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is a mystery story?
options: A story with a puzzle or secret to solve
questions.answer: A story with a puzzle or secret to solve
questions.hint: Think about detectives.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What do we call a small piece of information that helps solve a mystery?
questions.hint: Detectives look for these.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which question is good to ask BEFORE you start reading a mystery?
options: What do I think the mystery will be?
questions.answer: What do I think the mystery will be?
questions.hint: You have not read it yet.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which question is good to ask DURING reading?
options: Which clue have I just found?
What is the title of the next book?
How many pages did I read last week?
questions.answer: Which clue have I just found?
questions.hint: Think about what is happening now in the story.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which question is good to ask AFTER reading?
options: Was my guess about the mystery right?
questions.answer: Was my guess about the mystery right?
questions.hint: The story is finished.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Muddy paw prints lead from the kitchen to the garden. The cake is missing. Who probably took the cake?
questions.hint: Look at the prints.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: A detective finds sand in a boot. What might the clue tell her?
options: The owner went to the beach
questions.answer: The owner went to the beach
questions.hint: Where do you usually find sand?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Why should you keep track of clues as you read?
options: To help you solve the mystery
questions.answer: To help you solve the mystery

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: In a mystery, what is a 'suspect'?
options: Someone who might have done it
The person who wrote the story
questions.answer: Someone who might have done it
questions.hint: The detective is not sure about them yet.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Zara's pencil is missing. Her friend Leo has blue ink on his fingers, and Zara's pencil is blue. Is that enough to be sure Leo took it?
options: Yes, because Leo is her friend
questions.hint: One clue can have more than one explanation.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which word means to find the answer to a mystery?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: A window is open and the curtains are wet. What has probably happened?
options: Rain came in through the window
questions.answer: Rain came in through the window
questions.hint: Put the two clues together.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is a 'red herring' in a mystery story?
options: A clue that leads you the wrong way
questions.answer: A clue that leads you the wrong way
questions.hint: It tricks the reader.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Footprints in the snow are small and go to the shed. Who is most likely in the shed?
questions.hint: Small footprints belong to small feet.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Why do you think authors hide clues in mystery stories?
questions.hint: Think about how it feels to solve it yourself.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Write one question you could ask while reading a mystery story, and explain why it helps.
questions.hint: Start your question with 'Who', 'Why' or 'What'.

en_spell.topic: The /eɪ/ sound spelt ei, eigh and ey

questions.q: Which spelling is correct?
questions.hint: It means to find out how heavy something is.

questions.subject: en_spell

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: How do you spell the number 18 in words?

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: n_ _ghbour
questions.hint: It uses 'eigh' and ends in 'our'.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word means 'goods carried by a lorry, ship or train'?
questions.hint: It has the 'eigh' pattern.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word completes the sentence? 'Dogs should ___ their owners.'

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word completes the sentence? 'The owl hunted its ___ at night.'
questions.hint: It means an animal that is hunted.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which group of words all use 'eigh'?
questions.hint: Check every word in the group.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word does NOT belong with the others: they, grey, sleigh, obey?
questions.hint: Three of them share the same ending.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 5 misspelled words.
questions.answer: naybour → neighbour; grai → grey; obay → obey; aiteen → eighteen; thay → they
questions.text: On a cold winter night, our naybour took us for a ride in her sleigh. The sky was grai and the snow was deep. The horse had to obay every command. We counted aiteen stars before thay all hid behind the clouds. It was magical.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Write a sentence that uses two words from this list: sleigh, grey, they, weigh.
questions.hint: Check which spelling pattern each word uses.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which is the correct spelling of the word that means 'those people'?
questions.hint: It ends with the 'ey' pattern.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 4 misspelled words.
questions.answer: way → weigh; frait → freight; prai → prey; vain → vein
questions.text: At the market, the farmer had to way the apples on big scales. A lorry full of frait arrived at noon. A hawk circled above, looking for prai. I saw a blue vain on the farmer's strong hand. He said they would sell everything before lunch.
